page: Amazon Web Services m6idn.12xlarge is a general-purpose, network-optimized server instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It features a 3.5 GHz Intel Xeon 8375C processor offering 24 physical cores and 48 dedicated vCPUs with hyper-threading enabled. Memory capacity is configured at 192 GB of DDR4 RAM, establishing an industry-standard 4 GB per vCPU ratio. Storage is provisioned via 2850 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD capacity, providing direct-attached disk access for applications requiring low latency. Network connectivity is rated at a baseline bandwidth of 75 Gbps, supporting significant data transfer volume.

Benchmark evaluations show reliable performance profiles across varied compute and memory metrics. The platform achieves a Geekbench multi-core score of 15879.0 and single-core score of 1669.0, supplemented by strong image processing results reaching the top 25 percentile. In PassMark tests, hardware cryptographic acceleration via AES and VAES instruction sets yields strong scores of 43656.33, while overall CPU performance remains stable within average mid-tier bounds. Synthetic database operations score 21097.67 in PassMark, and in-memory Redis SET operations achieve 45.48 million transactions per second, supported by sustained memory bandwidth of 162.52 GB/sec on uncached reads.

Architecturally, the absence of dedicated GPU hardware limits high-throughput artificial intelligence inference, where generation speeds on large 70B parameter models reach 2.82 tokens per second. Additionally, local NVMe storage operates as ephemeral instance storage, requiring replication schemes for persistent state preservation. Despite these factors, the high density of dedicated x86 cores, balanced RAM allocation, robust 75 Gbps network fabric, and expansive local NVMe disk make this configuration effective for caching clusters, distributed databases, streaming ETL pipelines, and high-concurrency microservices.
description: Amazon Web Services m6idn.12xlarge is a balanced general-purpose instance powered by an Intel Xeon 8375C processor with 24 physical cores and 48 vCPUs running at 3.5 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The system integrates 192 GB of DDR4 memory, maintaining a 4:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio. Unlike diskless general-purpose instances, it includes 2850 GB of local NVMe SSD storage alongside a 75 Gbps baseline network interface. In benchmark assessments, the instance displays strong cryptographic execution via PassMark encryption tests and strong Geekbench image processing metrics, alongside solid multi-threaded performance across compilation and database operations. Without discrete GPUs, large-scale deep learning execution remains bounded by CPU limits. However, the combination of dedicated compute cores, large local NVMe storage capacity, and high network throughput makes this server well-aligned for high-throughput distributed caching, relational databases, real-time analytics pipelines, and data-intensive continuous integration tasks.
